newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - FEB 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - FEB 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou publicly pressured state banks yesterday for a further fall in interest rates, prompting the objections of the governor of the National Bank and president of the Union of Greek Banks Theodoros Karatzas, who said the reduction of high interest rates demanded action against the 'para-economy' and the reduction of the state's deficits.

--Brokerage firms dealing with foreign clients are facing a major problem as the daily limit on transactions has restricted their ability to work. The union of brokers has requested a quadrupling of the limit from the Cpaital Market Commission.

--The European Commission yesterday returned the issue of an energy tax to the relevant services for further examination: the tax, if imposed as seems likely, will have a strong effect on prices of fuel, electrical power and natural gas.
--The announcement yesterday that fuel prices will fall by 4.3 drachmas is expected to have positive effects on the economy and inflation.
--The transport ministry yesterday revealed increased fares for public transport and taxi tariffs as well as in post office charges.
--The next issue of Treasury bills will be by public subscription rather than auction and is expected to carry an interest rate of lower than 10.9 percent.
--The social security system, combatting unemployment, agriculture and shipping will be the first items on the agenda of the government's social dialogue, to be announced Friday.
--A partial floatation of Olympic Catering, owned by national carrier Olympic Airways, is in the offing, the transport minister announced yesterday.

--Olympic Catering's mooted listing on the Athens bourse leaves the road open for the floatation of the Olympic Airways Group. Sources said Olympic Catering would lay the ground for OA to enter the bourse.
--There will be no changes introduced to the country's social security system for this year to safeguard social calm, the government is reported to have told the EU.
--The finance ministry is examining how to best meet its budget targets of increasing the rate of tax revenues following January rates that fell short of targets.
--The national economy ministry is preparing a more flexible and effective system of export credits following the absorption of only six million dollars of an allocated 120 million in two years.
